title: Soybean Package of Practices, Sowing Methods & Girdle Beetle Control
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore
content: Soybean (Glycine max) is a premier Kharif oilseed and protein crop. Soil: Deep, well-drained clay loams (Black cotton soils) with pH 6.5 to 7.5. Sowing window: June 20 to July 10 following 100 mm accumulated monsoon rainfall. Avoid dry sowing. Sowing technique: Broad Bed Furrow (BBF) or Ridge and Furrow system is strongly recommended to prevent waterlogging during heavy rains and provide in-situ moisture conservation during dry spells. Seed rate: 65-75 kg/ha for germination >70%. Seed treatment: Treat with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS @ 2 g/kg seed, followed by Bradyrhizobium japonicum and PSB culture @ 5 g/kg seed. Spacing: 45 cm row spacing and 5-7 cm plant spacing at 3-4 cm depth. Major pest: Girdle beetle (Obereopsis brevis) girdles the stem, causing wilting of top leaves. Control: Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 0.3 ml/l or Thiacloprid 21.7 SC @ 1.5 ml/l at onset of attack.
